boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Kirksville record (August 6-9, 1862) in Operations North of Boston Mountains [August-November 1862]. The frozen interval runs to August 9, which NPS ties to another Union force finishing Porter's command three days later; that later action is known here only from McNeil's secondhand mention. The pursuit from July 29 is context. The live NPS campaign label ("Confederate Offensive North of Boston Mountains") does not replace the frozen campaign. Campaign-wide totals, marches and multi-action loss figures are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names a combined cavalry and artillery force against the Missouri Brigade; the live field reads 3,500 (US 1,000; CS 2,500), matching the NPS description. McNeil's August 7 report says Porter had 2,500 to 3,000 men in the houses and corn fields and that he had an aggregate of 1,000 with five guns; his September 17 report lists detachments by unit (the aggregate is left blank in print), says that after train guards, horse-holders, artillery supports and reserve he had about 500 men to engage, and that detachments joining the next day brought him to nearly 1,700. He also refers to Porter's 'entire force of 2,000' at Newark and an army of nearly 3,000 that had desolated the country.
claims.rationale: An aggregate, an engaged remainder and estimates of the enemy on different days. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: McNeil says Kirksville stands on a prairie ridge surrounded by timber and corn fields, open on the northeast from which he approached, ground he found highly favorable for attack; Porter had expelled the townspeople and occupied the houses. NPS says Porter's men hid in homes, stores and the crops of nearby fields.
claims.rationale: Ground described by an interested report and a summary; no map verification. Porter's occupation of the town preceded McNeil's arrival on the day of battle; phase unresolved.

claims.value: The frozen rows list Porter (Colonel) for the Confederates and McNeil (Colonel) for the Union; the live page styles McNeil Brigadier General. McNeil deployed on the northern and eastern faces of the town, putting Shaffer in charge of the right wing and Caldwell of the left. The inspected passages give no Confederate report; Porter appears only as the enemy commander.
claims.rationale: Command dispositions reported by one commander; no listed commander receives automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results are Union victory. McNeil says the town was taken after two hours and fifty minutes; NPS says after almost three hours. McNeil later heard at Bloomington that McFerran's forces had dispersed the rest of Porter's army; NPS says another Union force finished Porter's command three days later. That later action's own reports were not inspected.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: Frozen and live: 456 total (US 88; CS 368). McNeil's August 7 report gives 5 killed and 25 wounded, and enemy killed and wounded of 150 with 40 prisoners; his September report gives 5 killed and 32 wounded by the surgeon's report, and the enemy's loss as 150 killed, 300 to 400 wounded and 47 prisoners. He says 15 of the captured had been paroled before and that he had them shot.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The frozen US 88 is not found in the inspected passages and may cover a different population or the August 9 action; not established. Prisoners executed after capture are a distinct population from battle losses.

open_questions: Shaffer's and Benjamin's reports (located, not read), Caldwell's report, Surgeon Lyon's casualty report (not found in the volume), Schofield's general report, the reports of the August 9 action and maps remain deferred. No history covering Kirksville was found in Britton's volume I; this record has two families.

NPS/CWSAC is one family (the NPS battle page plus the frozen Arnold rows). Each Official Records report author is a separate family; the OR volume is a shared container, not a witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
